headline: X bundles Grok, Cursor, and X Premium into new multi-tier subscription plans
summary: X's new subscription offers tiers from $8 to $200/month, combining AI tools like Grok, coding assistance from Cursor, and X Premium features.
details: SpaceXSI, now known as X, has launched a unified "X Subscription" scheme. This new plan bundles access to Grok (AI), Cursor (coding), and X Premium features, depending on the chosen tier. The company recently acquired coding startup Cursor in August.

The entry-level "Plus" tier costs $8 per month for individuals. It includes Grok Chat, Voice, Imagine, and Build, along with Grok API and Cursor for coding. Subscribers also get X Premium features like a checkmark, fewer ads, enhanced creator tools, and advanced analytics.

For $30 per month, the "Premium" tier offers all Plus features plus Grok Bot and the latest Grok models. It also enables AI image and video creation via Grok, faster chat responses, and Cursor's code hosting, cloud agents, and automations. X benefits include ad-free scrolling and handle security.
The "Super" tier, priced at $100 per month, includes everything from the Plus and Premium plans. A key benefit of this tier is priority access to Grok models during peak usage times.

The highest tier, "Ultra," costs $200 per month and provides the earliest access to all products and models. It also offers 20 times the usage capacity of the Plus tier. Premium, Super, and Ultra plans are also available for teams, with customized plans for enterprise customers.

headline_marked: [[Flock Safety camera costs]] for cities can balloon to over $200,000 annually
headline: Flock Safety camera costs for cities can balloon to over $200,000 annually
summary: Public records reveal how Flock Safety's surveillance camera contracts with cities like Covington and Alpharetta, Georgia, have rapidly escalated, with annual costs reaching hundreds of thousands of dollars.
details: Covington, Georgia's police department saw its annual payments to Flock Safety surge from $40,000 in 2020 to over $201,000 by August 2026. This dramatic increase highlights a national trend of escalating costs for surveillance technology.
The initial $40,000 covered 20 cameras. By 2022, the cost more than doubled to $81,250 with the addition of 15 new "Falcon" license plate reader cameras and their installation.

Further expansion in 2024 saw payments reach $113,225, including maintenance for 35 cameras and eight new Falcon units. In 2025, Covington committed $159,000, adding Flock's "Drone as First Responder" program to its services.

Alpharetta, Georgia, experienced a similar pattern, with its annual Flock bill ballooning from $17,680 in 2020 to $381,000 by 2025. Many cities initially gained access to Flock cameras already purchased by homeowner associations.

Flock Safety expands contracts through various incentives, including multiyear discounts and free trials for new products like Nova. They also offer upgrades to comprehensive platforms like the Elite Package of FlockOS.

Experts warn that once police departments adopt such tools, it becomes politically challenging to remove them, leading to long-term financial commitments for taxpayers. WIRED obtained these documents via public records requests.
